name: Kitchen Dispatch Simulator
desc:
A dark kitchen has cooks cooks, numbered from 1. You are given events, a list of strings sorted by time (an integer number of minutes):

  • "t ORDER id duration vip": order id arrives at time t; it takes duration minutes to cook; vip is 1 for a VIP order, else 0.
  • "t CANCEL id": the customer cancels order id at time t.

Simulate the kitchen:

  • Every cook is free at time 0. A cook who starts an order at time s is busy until s + duration and is free again at that exact time.
  • As soon as a cook is free and an order is waiting, the cook starts an order immediately. The waiting order chosen is: VIP orders first, then the earliest arrival, then the smallest id. The cook chosen is the one who has been free for the longest time (earliest time at which they became free), then the smallest number.
  • A cancelled order that is still waiting is removed from the queue. A cancelled order that is being cooked is stopped: its cook is free at the time of the cancellation. Cancelling an order that is finished, already cancelled or unknown does nothing.
  • At a given time, first the cooks who finish at that time become free, then the events of that time are applied in the order of the list, and only then cooks pick orders.

Your task is to return, for every order sorted by id, [id, cook, start, end]: the cook who cooked it and the times when cooking started and ended. Use -1 for cook, start and end when the order was cancelled before starting, and -1 for end only when it was cancelled while being cooked.

Example

For cooks = 2, events = ["0 ORDER 1 10 0", "0 ORDER 2 5 0", "1 ORDER 3 4 0", "2 ORDER 4 6 1", "3 CANCEL 3", "5 ORDER 5 1 0", "8 CANCEL 1", "20 CANCEL 2"], the output should be

[[1, 1, 0, -1], [2, 2, 0, 5], [3, -1, -1, -1], [4, 2, 5, 11], [5, 1, 8, 9]]
[execution time limit] 4 seconds (py3)
[memory limit] 1 GB
[input] integer cooks
[input] array.string events
[output] array.array.integer
howto:
Où écrire
  1. Écris dans l'éditeur à droite, fichier solution.py.
  2. Complète la fonction solution(cooks, events). Garde son nom et ses paramètres : ce sont les tests qui l'appellent, avec leurs propres données. N'écris pas d'appel à la fonction toi-même.
Ce que tu dois renvoyer
  1. Ta fonction doit renvoyer le résultat avec return. Un print ne compte pas : il sort seulement dans l'onglet Console Output.
  2. Ici, la valeur attendue est une liste : compare ce que tu renvoies à « Expected return value » dans les résultats.
  3. La comparaison est exacte (même type, mêmes valeurs, même ordre dans une liste), sauf les nombres décimaux, comparés à 0,000001 près.
Lancer et vérifier
  1. Clique RUN TESTS (ou Ctrl + Entrée) : tes 2 tests visibles tournent.
  2. Quand c'est bon, tu vois en vert « Tests passed: 2/2. ». Sinon, ouvre le test marqué Wrong answer : compare « Expected return value » et « Your return value », et clique VIEW DIFF pour colorer les cases différentes. Runtime error veut dire que ton code a planté : le message est dans le test.
  3. Clique SUBMIT : ta note sur 100 compte aussi 10 tests cachés. Soumets dès que quelques tests passent, puis améliore et resoumets : c'est la dernière soumission qui compte.
